newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Second Shi'ite dies after attack in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Second Shi'ite dies after attack in Pakistan.

text.p: A Shi'ite Moslem activist died in hospital on Sunday from bullet wounds received in an apparent sectarian attack in the city of Multan, in Pakistan's central province of Punjab, doctors said.
They said they had been unable to save the life of Makhdoom Sabtain Raza, hit by nine bullets in Saturday's shooting.
Masked gunmen on a motorcycle fired on three local leaders of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan organisation, killing one on the spot and badly wounding the others.
The three Shi'ites were attacked after they had attended a marriage ceremony in the city's Lal Shah district. Doctors said the third wounded man remained in critical condition.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for what appeared to be the latest act in a vendetta between rival Sunni and Shi'ite Moslem groups in Pakistan.
At least eight people have been killed in the feud in southern Punjab in the past 13 days.
Shi'ite activists have in the past blamed such attacks on the militant Sunni Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan group.
Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over religious doctrine have often spilled into violence in Pakistan, where Shi'ites make up about 15 percent of the predominantly Sunni Population.
